newsitem.title: USA: IBM posts third quarter income of $1.3 billion.
newsitem.headline: IBM posts third quarter income of $1.3 billion.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp. said Monday it earned $1.3 billion in the third quarter, up from a loss of $500 million a year ago when it was paying for its acquisition of Lotus Development Corp.
IBM said its income meant earnings of $2.45 a share, just above Wall Street's average estimate of $2.43, and came on revenue of $18.1 billion, which was 8 percent ahead of a year earlier.
IBM's shares retreated slightly in pre-opening trade in New York, falling $1.625 to $127.75 a share. However, the shares had gained $3.75 to $129.375 Friday in anticipation of the earnings report.

"This was a very good quarter," said Louis V. Gerstner, chairman. "A highlight was the continued rollout of integrated solutions that help fulfil the promise of a networked world to our customers," he said.
The company said revenues were higher in North America, Asia and Latin America but were flat in Europe. Revenue at its services division increased by 26 percent, IBM said.

In the third quarter of 1995, excluding the costs of the Lotus acquisition, IBM earned $1.3 billion, or $2.30 a share, and had revenue of $16.8 billion. The one-time charge related to its acquisition of Lotus was $1.8 billion.
